scenes.title: Introducing the Unit Circle
scenes.visual: A 2D Cartesian coordinate grid with labeled X and Y axes centered on screen. A bright circle of radius 2 units labeled 'Unit Circle (r=1)' fades in. A point P starts at (2,0) on the rightmost edge of the circle, with a radial line segment connecting the origin (0,0) to P.
scenes.narration: The unit circle is simply a circle centered at the origin with a radius of one. As a point moves around this circle, its position defines the trigonometric functions sine and cosine.

scenes.title: Decomposing into Coordinates
scenes.visual: The point P rests at an angle of 45 degrees. A right-angled triangle forms inside the circle with vertices at the origin, (x,0), and P. The horizontal leg along the x-axis is highlighted in cyan labeled 'cos(θ)', and the vertical leg is highlighted in yellow labeled 'sin(θ)'. An arc angle θ is shown near the origin.
scenes.narration: At any angle theta, the horizontal distance from the origin to the point is the cosine of theta, while the vertical distance is the sine of theta.

scenes.title: Tracing Sine and Cosine Waves
scenes.visual: The screen splits into two panels. On the left, the unit circle with point P rotates continuously. On the right, two axes appear: a yellow sine wave plot at the top and a cyan cosine wave plot at the bottom. Dashed horizontal lines project from P to trace the yellow sine wave, while vertical projections trace the cyan cosine wave in real time.
scenes.narration: As the point continuously rotates around the circle, tracking its vertical height traces out a smooth sine wave, while tracking its horizontal position traces out a cosine wave.
